subject.declared_domain: The write path by which the incremental_updater Lambda materializes the branch-head freshness marker -- a single S3 JSON object recording, per Iceberg table, the current snapshot_id, metadata_location and last_write_iso. Covers stamp_branch_head_marker (:567-587) and the _provenance.stamp_marker machinery it delegates to. It does NOT cover this file's Iceberg write path (carded separately as W3-thav), and it does not cover the OTHER writers that stamp the same object -- derive_runner and cse_store also call stamp_marker, and this card makes no claim about their behaviour.

methodology.how: After a Nessie commit lands, the handler calls stamp_branch_head_marker (:730) inside its own try/except. That function is a pure arg-adapter (:583-587): it passes the pyiceberg catalog, the writer_id literal 'incremental_updater', the warehouse bucket derived from WAREHOUSE_URI (:548-550), and a FOUR-TABLE TUPLE LITERAL ('graph_nodes','graph_edges','graph_contracts','cse') into _provenance.stamp_marker. stamp_marker (_provenance.py:194-233) resolves EACH named table's current snapshot from the catalog, builds a marker dict, and dispatches on _cas_enabled(): CAS path if the env flag is on, otherwise _stamp_unconditional. ⛔ THE BOUND IS THE TUPLE, AND IT NAMES THREE TABLES THIS LAMBDA NEVER WRITES. graph_edges, graph_contracts and cse are written by other producers entirely; this path reads their snapshots and publishes freshness metadata about them.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: NOTHING THAT REACHES THE CALLER, BY DESIGN. stamp_marker never raises to its caller (_provenance.py:199-201), and the handler additionally wraps the call in its own try/except that logs MARKER_STAMP_FAIL at WARNING (:731-732). Inside stamp_marker there are three distinct silent outcomes: a table that fails to resolve is logged at WARN and omitted (:219-220); if NO table resolves the function returns None having written nothing (:221-222); and if the existing marker's committed_at_iso is >= ours the write is SKIPPED with an INFO line (:256-258). All three leave the previous object in place, and a reader of that object cannot tell any of them from a healthy stamp that simply has not happened yet.
silent_degrade_paths: ⛔ THE ARCHIVE THAT WAS RULED BLOCKING HAS NEVER EXECUTED. _archive_superseded (_provenance.py:271-303) preserves the marker about to be overwritten, and its docstring records that CTO ruled it BLOCKING on the merge landing (:279-280). MEASURED: it is called ONLY from _stamp_cas, never from _stamp_unconditional; _cas_enabled (:236-239) defaults to 'off'; the live Lambda's environment contains no GLOBGRPH_MARKER_CAS variable; and warehouse/_branch_head.history/ holds ZERO objects and does not appear in the bucket's prefix listing. So on a non-versioned, destructively-overwritten object, every superseded marker in this system's history is unrecoverable -- which is precisely the condition :276-278 says the archive exists to prevent.

The wholesale-replace clobber remains live in the running code even though THIS writer does not currently trigger it. Any writer of this object that passes a shorter tuple erases the rows it omits, silently, and the result is a well-formed marker that simply lacks a table. Nothing in the object records which writer dropped what.
A table-name resolution failure omits that table's row (:219-220) and the stamp still succeeds. An omitted row is byte-identical in the object to a row erased by the clobber above.

The monotonicity guard (:256) skips the write when an existing marker is not-older. That is correct behaviour, but it means a clock skew between writers, or a writer with a fast clock, can cause a genuinely newer stamp to be silently discarded with only an INFO line.

_nessie_main_hash (:553-564) is best-effort; on failure the marker's nessie_commit_hash silently falls back to graph_nodes' snapshot_id (_provenance.py:223). A consumer reading that field cannot tell a real Nessie hash from the fallback without checking its shape.

A marker failure never fails the batch (:729-732), so the marker can be stale while every commit is landing perfectly. The marker is the freshness oracle, and the thing it cannot report is its own failure to be written.
failure_mode.evidence: THE ARCHIVE FINDING WAS EXERCISED ON THREE INDEPENDENT PLANES, each capable of returning the opposite answer. PLANE 1 (code, deployed copy not source): parsed the vendored _provenance.py's :242-268 and :305-390 separately -- '_archive_superseded' appears in the _stamp_cas body and does NOT appear in the _stamp_unconditional body. PLANE 2 (live configuration): aws lambda get-function-configuration returns four environment variables -- SNS_TOPIC_ARN, NESSIE_URI, WAREHOUSE_URI, AWS_REGION_OVERRIDE -- and GLOBGRPH_MARKER_CAS is not among them, so _cas_enabled reads its 'off' default and the unconditional branch is the one that runs. PLANE 3 (the artifact): warehouse/_branch_head.history/ returns no contents, and the prefix is absent from the bucket's delimiter listing, which independently returned ten real sibling prefixes -- so the instrument demonstrably reports prefixes that do exist. Three planes, three different ways to be wrong, one answer. ⚠ A BOUND I WILL NOT OVERSTATE: an empty prefix on a non-versioned bucket cannot by itself distinguish 'never written' from 'written and later deleted'. The code plane is what closes it -- the only caller of the archive is on a branch the live configuration does not select. I did not run the CAS path and make no claim about whether it would work if enabled.

verdict.why: This path does what it claims and I verified the claim that mattered most. It stamped the live marker 52 minutes before this carding; its bound is a call-site literal tuple of exactly four tables; and the erasure hazard its own module documents -- a short-tuple writer wiping rows for tables it does not write -- is measurably NOT firing here, evidenced by cse's last_write_iso surviving 2h22m older than the stamp that rewrote the object. The fix at :575-582 is exercised, not merely committed. I also closed the deployed-vs-source question by content rather than by filename: the vendored _provenance.py is 6,557 real bytes behind the tree, but the divergence begins at line 405 and every symbol this card cites sits in a byte-identical region, so these citations describe running code. QUALIFIED rather than SOUND on three measured defects: (1) the superseded-marker archive that CTO ruled BLOCKING has never executed once -- it is reachable only from the CAS path, CAS is off by default, the live function sets no override, and the history prefix is empty; on a destructively-overwritten object with versioning locked off, that makes every prior marker state unrecoverable; (2) the wholesale-replace clobber is still live in the running code and this path's safety from it rests entirely on one literal tuple that nothing reconciles against the namespace's real table set; (3) the failure surface is silent in every direction -- an unresolvable table, a total resolution failure, and a monotonicity skip all leave the previous object in place and are indistinguishable, in the artifact, from a healthy stamp that has not fired yet. Not UNSOUND: nothing measured shows a wrong value published, the monotonicity guard and the never-fail-the-commit precedence are both correct, and the four live rows are internally consistent across three clocks. NOT INCOMPLETE: all 7 rows worked, every scalar 'measured'. ⛔ NO COMPLETENESS CLAIM ON THE WRITER POPULATION for this object, per CCY3-AC7 -- I know three writer families exist and did not establish they are all. ⛔ NO FORWARD DISPOSITION. Per QUALIFY-DO-NOT-FIX nothing was fixed: the CAS flag was not flipped, no env var was set, and this lane committed nothing to _provenance.py or to the Lambda.
blocking_defects: For anyone who would need to show what a previous branch-head marker held -- to adjudicate a freshness FAIL, or to reconstruct a clobber: no prior state exists. The archive ruled BLOCKING at _provenance.py:279-280 is unreachable on the default path, and warehouse/_branch_head.history/ is empty. A criterion comparing against a prior marker degrades from FAIL to UN-EVALUABLE, which is the exact outcome :276-278 was written to prevent. Owner: _provenance.py's owner for the structure; UNOWNED for the decision to leave CAS off.

For any writer of warehouse/_branch_head.main.json: the wholesale-replace at _provenance.py:242-268 is live, so a shorter tuple silently erases the omitted tables' rows. This path is safe only because :585 happens to carry all four names, and nothing checks that tuple against the namespace. Owner: each writer's seat for its own tuple.

For anyone using this marker as a health signal: a marker failure cannot fail the batch, an unresolvable table is omitted rather than raised, and a not-newer stamp is skipped at INFO. A stale marker is not evidence of a failed commit, and a complete-looking marker is not evidence that every table resolved. Owner 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp.

For anyone reading nessie_commit_hash: on a Nessie REST failure it silently falls back to graph_nodes' snapshot_id (_provenance.py:223), and the field does not record which it is. Owner: _provenance.py's owner.
